conviction_note: abs_move 11.5 (implied 10.5, median of 8 prints 14.1, a first Q4 guide is likely) times (2*56/100-1): the print turns on the Q4 EBITDA guide, HRC spot ran +$40/t through Sept-Oct and both EAF peers confirmed higher Q3 ASPs, but the option market already pays for upside (skew -12.5) and the Stelco idling plus peer cost inflation cut the other way, so the lean is small; impact_sum (+0.8) and the scaled number (+1.4) agree in sign and scale.
bar: Company guide: Q3 2026 adjusted EBITDA 'approximately $575 million', shipments +~300kt vs Q2's 4.025Mt (>4.3Mt), ASP +$55/t vs Q2's $1,124 (8-K ex-99.1 2026-07-23, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000764065/000076406526000097/clf-202606308xkex991.htm; call: https://www.manufacturingdive.com/news/cleveland-cliffs-offers-bright-q3-2026-outlook-despite-maintenance-outages/826130/). Street: revenue ~$5.72B (sweep and https://www.benzinga.com/node/62267494 agree), EPS $0.19-0.25 across sources (Benzinga $0.24, opencapital $0.25, sweep $0.19-0.24). The guide-implied revenue (4.3Mt x ~$1,179 plus ~$0.7B non-steel) is ~$5.8B, ~1-2% above the $5.72B consensus, which is the basis of print_vs_bar.
positioning_check: Short interest 78.52M shares at the 2026-09-30 FINRA settlement, ~13.8% of shares outstanding, 4.67 days to cover (https://equibles.com/stocks/clf/shortinterest, fetched 2026-10-16 by the sweep; the 10-15 settlement is not published until ~10-24). Baseline skew -12.48 vol points (upside paid), put/call OI 0.59, ATM IV 104.5%, event-implied move 10.5%. Tape: 20d -2.4%, 5d -6.0%; CLF closed 12.19 (10-08) -> 12.98 (10-09, +6.5% on 24.8M shares) -> 12.86 (10-13) -> 12.58 (10-14) -> 12.15 (10-15, -3.4% on 24.3M) while STLD went 234.17 -> 240.76 and NUE 246.14 -> 254.69 over the same sessions (Yahoo chart v8, https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/CLF?range=1mo&interval=1d). Both legs are CLF-specific and no news attaches to either. A 13.8% short with upside-paid skew says a positive guide would squeeze; a negative needs to explain why that mechanism fails.

findings.finding: US HRC spot rose through the whole of Q3 and into Q4: Nucor's weekly CSP went from $1,190/st (2026-09-08) to $1,220 (09-28) to $1,230 (10-05) with lead times held at 3-5 weeks, SMU's average was $1,225/st on 09-08 and Kallanish put domestic HRC at $1,210-1,220/st on 10-02, against the ~$1,150/t level CLF's July call cited; the Q2 release said Q4 EBITDA will 'even further exceed' the ~$575M Q3 guide, and a higher Q4 number than the July framing is what the spot series implies.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last print (2026-07-23, +15.98%) rose on the Q3 EBITDA guide despite an EPS miss (https://finviz.com/news/371803/cleveland-cliffs-shares-jump-as-upbeat-third-quarter-forecast-outweighs-earnings-miss-nyse-clf); 2025-10-20 +21.47% and 2026-02-09 -16.43% were also guide-driven. This name pays, in both directions, on the forward guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the skew is upside-paid (-12.5) and Wells Fargo upgraded on 10-06 on exactly this logic. Not fully priced: 13 analysts sit at Hold with a $12.60 mean target against a $12.15 spot (https://ca.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/CLEVELAND-CLIFFS-INC-50916560/consensus/), the stock is 24.6% off its high and gave back its whole pre-print rally in the two sessions before the seal; if the market held a Q4 guide materially above $575M the stock would not be sitting on a mean target 4% away.
findings.independence: Nucor's 2026-09-17 Q3 guide cites 'higher average selling prices and stable volumes' at steel mills (https://www.steelorbis.com/steel-news/latest-news/nucor-issues-q3-2026-earnings-guidance-expects-higher-steel-mills-and-steel-products-earnings-1478837.htm); Steel Dynamics' 2026-09-17 guide expects 'average realized steel selling values to increase' and says low customer inventories 'continue to support favorable pricing conditions' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001022671/000110465926108777/tm2625690d1_ex99-1.htm); Wells Fargo 2026-10-06 OW/$14 on 2027 EBITDA $2.65B above consensus (https://www.itiger.com/news/1196432764).

findings.finding: Both EAF peers' mid-quarter guides (2026-09-17) missed consensus on costs: Nucor guided $5.55-5.65 vs ~$6.17 citing 'higher costs of products sold' and no repeat of a $130M Q2 refund, Steel Dynamics $5.34-5.38 vs ~$5.99, and both fell ~5% on the day; CLF's July guide assumed 'slightly lower' Q3 costs, so a cost-side miss against the $575M is the live risk the peers flag.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-04-20 (-2.11%) fell on an $80M energy-cost spike despite a beat (https://insights.munich-startup.de/news/feed/cleveland-cliffs-shares-drop-5-despite-q1-earnings-beat-as-80m-energy-cost-spike-weighs-on-profitability); a cost miss on the reported quarter has been sold before, but modestly.
findings.why_not_priced: The peer guides are a month old and the steel group has since recovered (NUE 236 -> 255, STLD 226 -> 241 from 10-01); CLF's own consensus EPS ($0.19-0.25) still brackets the guide-implied number, so nobody has cut for costs. Proxy: CLF is integrated with its own iron ore and does not buy scrap at Nucor's scale, so the transmission is partial and the company has not confirmed it.
findings.independence: Steel Dynamics 8-K 2026-09-17 says fabrication margins were hit by 'increased steel input material costs' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001022671/000110465926108777/tm2625690d1_ex99-1.htm). STLD reports after the close on 2026-10-19, inside this window, so its actual cost line lands on the 10-20 session.

findings.finding: Stelco is indefinitely idling its Hamilton cold-rolled and coated lines from 2026-10-09 (350-500 layoffs), its president's 2026-10-09 letter to Ottawa says continued production of those products is loss-making with demand down ~25% vs the 2024 quarterly average and Canadian CR/coated exports to the US down 58%, Canada's industry minister has threatened court action under the Investment Canada Act with her lawyers 'reviewing' the reply and the CEO saying he will fight it in court; the July release had said Stelco was 'positioned to return to generating significant earnings', so the Stelco contribution inside the $575M and the Q4 guide is weaker than July framed, and a restructuring charge or a Canadian filing could land in the window.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The idling itself cost the stock 9% on 2026-09-28 (https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/09/28/cleveland-cliffs-sinks-9-as-selloff-outruns-steel-group-nucor-and-steel-dynamics-pull-back/) and was recovered by 10-05 (+10%); Stelco commentary on prior prints has not been the line the stock traded on.
findings.why_not_priced: The idling announcement is priced (the 9% drop and the recovery). What is not: no 8-K has been filed and no charge has been quantified, the company says tonnage is unchanged but has not said what the Q3 Stelco EBITDA was, and the government's legal decision has no date. Sized net of the rest of the company: Stelco is roughly 15% of shipments and the idled lines are a fraction of that, while the US mills carry the quarter; the 13.8% short and upside-paid skew argue for keeping this small.
findings.independence: Algoma Steel's 2026-10-01 Q3 guide: shipments ~145kt and adjusted EBITDA C$-10M to C$-20M, mostly a power outage but with 'a less favourable sales mix' (https://www.steelorbis.com/steel-news/latest-news/algoma-steel-expects-negative-adjusted-ebitda-in-q3-on-power-outage-impact-1481453.htm); company announcement of the idling 2026-09-29 (https://www.miningweekly.com/article/cleveland-cliffs-to-idle-output-at-canada-steel-plant-blames-tariffs-2026-09-29); minister's five-day deadline (https://www.insauga.com/industry-minister-presses-stelcos-u-s-owner-to-present-job-saving-plan-in-5-days/).

findings.finding: Detroit-three Q3 2026 US sales were weak (GM 670,974, -6%; Ford 509,764, -6.6%; Stellantis 324,277, flat) and Omdia's North American Q3 production tracker ran about -0.6% y/y, while CLF's July guide assigned about half of its ~300kt sequential Q3 shipment increase to automotive (29% of Q2 steelmaking revenue).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Automotive volume has not been the line prior prints traded on; Q2's auto shipments were the highest in two years and the stock still traded on the guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Proxy, not a company number: the sequential increase CLF guided is against a Q2 depressed by April-May outages, so a y/y sales decline does not refute it, and the company's own statement (Q2 auto shipments highest in two years, finishing lines 'full') is the more direct series and points the other way. Filed small for that reason.
findings.independence: Omdia July 2026 tracker: 3Q output 'pacing lower' (https://omdia.tech.informa.com/om145787/north-america-vehicle-production-tracker-3q--july-2026); CLF call 2026-07-23 for the automotive share of the shipment increase (https://www.industryweek.com/leadership/companies-executives/news/55393737/cleveland-cliffs-sees-much-stronger-second-half-more-growth-into-27).

findings.finding: Management said on the Q2 call that resetting fixed-price (largely automotive) contracts signed at ~$800/t to the ~$1,150/t-plus market is 'a foregone conclusion' worth about $500M of EBITDA year over year and that 2027 adjusted EBITDA could reach $3.3B; the Q3 call is the first since contract negotiations for 2027 began and a quantified 2027 reset is the kind of line this name has paid for.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Forward-year framing moved the stock on 2026-02-09 (-16.43%, '26 outlook below expectations) and 2026-07-23 (+15.98%); the name trades on the forward number.
findings.why_not_priced: The $3.3B figure is three months old and the mean target is $12.60 on a Hold consensus, so the Street has not underwritten it; Wells Fargo's 10-06 upgrade ($2.65B 2027 EBITDA 'above FactSet consensus', $500M from contract repricing) is the only house that has, and it moved the stock ~1%. If a dated, quantified reset were in the price the consensus 2027 number would already sit near $2.65B.
findings.independence: Wells Fargo 2026-10-06 (https://www.itiger.com/news/1196432764). Note this finding and finding 1 both rest on HRC being higher than July assumed; they are different lines (Q4 guide vs 2027 contracts) but not independent evidence.

findings.finding: CLF-specific tape into the print: +6.5% on 2026-10-09 (24.8M shares) with no news, then -2.2% and -3.4% on 10-14/10-15 (24M shares) while NUE and STLD rose, leaving the stock at 12.15-12.20 with 78.5M shares (13.8%) short, 4.67 days to cover and options skew paying for upside.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The two largest prior up-moves (+21.47% 2025-10-20, +15.98% 2026-07-23) came into a stock that was heavily shorted; the squeeze is a mechanism of its own on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: The pre-print rally has been unwound, so there is less to sell on a merely in-line print; the short base has not covered (last settlement 09-30). An unexplained move is not evidence of direction and is sized near zero; the positioning facts are what carry the small positive.
findings.independence: Short interest from https://equibles.com/stocks/clf/shortinterest (2026-09-30 settlement); peer closes from https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/STLD?range=1mo&interval=1d and https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/NUE?range=1mo&interval=1d.

findings.finding: Two new capital projects since the last print: a $1B Middletown Works investment backed by a $500M DOE award (2026-08-21) and a $200M Butler Works GOES expansion with a $75M DOE award showcased to the Energy Secretary on 2026-10-06; the 2026 capex guide is still ~$700M and a 2027 capex frame above that, if given on the call, would weigh on the free-cash-flow and sub-2.5x leverage story the stock is partly valued on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-04-20 (-2.11%) traded partly on $7.25B of long-term debt and negative FCF (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/cleveland-cliffs-drops-5-despite-142748272.html); the balance sheet is a line this stock has sold on.
findings.why_not_priced: Both announcements are public and the DOE share is grant money, so most of this is priced; what is not is a 2027 capex number, which the company usually gives in February rather than October, hence the small size.
findings.independence: Company release list (https://www.clevelandcliffs.com/news/news-releases) for the 2026-08-21 Middletown and 2026-10-05 Butler items; 2026 capex guide of ~$700M in the Q2 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000764065/000076406526000097/clf-202606308xkex991.htm).

findings.finding: AISI raw steel output for the week ending 2026-10-10 was 1.796Mt at 77.8% utilisation, +4.1% y/y, with year-to-date production +5.3% at 79.0% average utilisation and the Great Lakes region (CLF's core) at 534kt; industry volume ran above last year through the whole of Q3, consistent with CLF's >4.3Mt shipment guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Shipment volume alone has not been the line prior prints traded on.
findings.why_not_priced: Industry proxy, published weekly and widely read; it corroborates the guide rather than beating it, so it carries little size.
findings.independence: Scrap Monster report of the same AISI release (https://www.scrapmonster.com/news/steel/u.s.-raw-steel-production-report-output-up-4.1-yoy-aisi-2026-10-13/100236); Steel Dynamics guided 'record shipments' for Q3 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001022671/000110465926108777/tm2625690d1_ex99-1.htm).

outside_window.finding: Nucor reports Q3 after the close on 2026-10-26, the first full peer print on sheet pricing and costs after CLF's; its read-through lands a week after this window.
The FINRA 2026-10-15 short-interest settlement (whether the 78.5M short base built or covered into the print) is published around 2026-10-24.

searched_and_found_nothing: No cause found for the CLF-specific +6.5% on 2026-10-09 or the -5.5% over 2026-10-14/15 (news searches by date, analyst-action searches, Quiver items: the 'slides 4.3%' piece is dated 2026-06-08).

No 8-K since the 07-24 item 5.02 (CFO promoted to President): EDGAR submissions show only an SD (09-18), a 13G (08-07) and two Form 4s on 10-02, both director retainer share elections (Bloom, Cronin; 3,487 shares each at $11.47), not open-market trades.
No POSCO definitive agreement or asset-sale (Toledo HBI, FPT) news since the July call said no deal was imminent on valuation.
No October 2026 US-Canada or US-Mexico Section 232 deal; latest reporting is August talks with no agreement.
No published Q3 adjusted EBITDA consensus (FactSet/Visible Alpha/TIKR) reachable; the $575M guide is the only EBITDA bar.

No Nucor CSP letter for 2026-10-12 found; the series ends at $1,230 on 10-05. No SMU/Argus/Fastmarkets HRC assessment for 10-13 to 10-16 reachable (mysteel price cells blank, nasdaq/benzinga pages 403/503).
No October 2026 analyst preview beyond the Wells Fargo 10-06 upgrade; no downgrade in the week before the print.
No Canadian court filing against Cleveland-Cliffs as of 2026-10-13 reporting; the minister's office said lawyers were reviewing the 10-09 letter.

baseline_tension: The findings lean the same way as the skew (upside paid) and against the 5-day drop; because the option market already leans up, the HRC/guide finding is sized below what the series alone would justify and p_up sits close to 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 7 (positioning is the thing to beat): the HRC/guide finding agrees with the upside-paid skew, so it is partly in the price; cut from +2.5 to +2.0 and p_up from 57 to 56.

Rule 5 (narrow proxy loses to the company's own number): peer cost pressure cut from -1.0 to -0.7 and the auto-sales proxy from -0.5 to -0.3, because CLF's own July statements (costs slightly lower, auto shipments highest in two years) are the more direct series and were filed as independence.
Rules 7 and 9 (crowded short; net of the rest of the company): Stelco cut from -1.5 to -1.0, sized net of the ~85% of shipments from the US mills and against a 13.8% short with upside-paid skew.
Rule 5 (an unexplained drawdown is not evidence): the tape finding cut from +0.5 to +0.3; only the positioning facts carry it.

Rule 6 (bar and window): bar stated against the company guide plus two agreeing revenue sources; Nucor's 10-26 print and the 10-15 FINRA settlement moved to outside_window; capex finding trimmed to -0.2 because a 2027 capex guide normally lands in February.
Rule 1 (reaction history has veto): left standing; this name's last three large moves were all on the guide, so the guidance findings keep their sign and the reported-quarter findings stay small.
